evaluation_protocol.query_accounting: shot_cost(0) = 1, shot_cost(n) = n for n >= 1 (total = sum(n * N_n) + N_0)
evaluation_protocol.depth_cap: max Grover depth <= n_max for every track (enforced by the evaluators and the CI oracle)

entries.name: OnDemand-UltraLean (Bhattacharyya Tie-Breaker)
entries.description: Lean-mid / strong-shallow baseline schedule on the plain r=1.45 geometric ladder (top_tuple=(2,2,2,1,1), s_shallow=0.65) combined with Fisher-adaptive local-minimum basin detection and on-demand boundary-regularized Bhattacharyya (eps=0.04) tie-breaking shots over step-1 upper integer depths.

entries.name: 3R-Cond (r=1.50 Opposite-Slope + Tie-Breaker)
entries.description: Two/three-round conditional semi-adaptive parallel amplitude estimation using a top-down r=1.50 geometric ladder with lean Round-1 shot ramp (slope=0.85), Round-2 complementary opposite-slope phase steering (+-phi_0) with Bhattacharyya rival-aware depth selection and conditional rival-killer shots, and a conditional Round-3 tie-breaker (triggered on ~4% of trials when Delta_ell_2 < 4.5).

entries.name: mlqae-plain (Labib 2026)
entries.description: Non-adaptive geometric Grover depth ladder round(1.45^j) up to n_max with untuned linear-decay canonical shot ramp (N_j = L - j) and exact global maximum-likelihood estimation (Labib 2026, arXiv:2609.02715).

entries.name: MLQAE-GaussCent (Flagship + Local Gaussian Centroid)
entries.description: Non-adaptive flagship geometric Grover schedule (r=1.45 plus near-cap mirror-breaking rung at round(nmax/1.3) with canonical linear shot profile) paired with a two-stage continuous terminal estimator: exact coarse-grid global maximum likelihood + 25-point parabolic zoom to identify the winning basin mode, followed by fine-grid Gaussian-windowed local posterior centroid integration over [-0.75w, +0.75w] (c = 4.5 sigma_theta) around the mode. Smoothly averages skew and near-tied mirror modes while exponentially suppressing distant rival basins, reducing both C95 and C99 relative to global ML at zero extra query cost.

entries.name: mlqae-flagship (Labib 2026)
entries.description: Flagship non-adaptive schedule of Labib (2026, arXiv:2609.02715): ratio r=1.45 geometric Grover depth ladder plus one degeneracy-breaking cap rung at round(n_max / 1.3), cutting C99 by 16-20% and achieving C95_seq = 0.21.

entries.name: BAE-Adaptive (Ramoa & Santos 2024)
entries.description: Annealed Bayesian Amplitude Estimation (Ramoa & Santos 2024, arXiv:2401.15072): online Bayesian posterior tracking with annealed depth selection 2n+1 ~ c / sigma_theta and PGH step-ratio cap.

entries.name: chebAE (Rall & Fuller 2023)
entries.description: Chebyshev Amplitude Estimation (Rall & Fuller 2023, Quantum 7, 937; arXiv:2207.08628): adaptive Chebyshev degree selection with Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals, late-stage single-shot stepping (nu=8), and polynomial inversion.

entries.name: csAE (Labib et al. 2024)
entries.description: Compressed-Sensing Amplitude Estimation (Labib et al. 2024, arXiv:2405.14697): power-of-two Grover depth schedule (largest 2^k <= n_max) with the C = 4.0 shot ramp, sliding-window sign recovery, 2q-th order virtual uniform linear array (ULA) covariance construction, and ESPRIT frequency estimation; run through the self-contained leaderboard submission.
entries.evaluation_note: Evaluated through leaderboard/submissions/csae_esprit_labib on the holdout trials (20,000 per scale); powers of two up to the largest 2^k <= n_max, so scales 540 and 1000 share the depth-512 schedule.

entries.name: BIQAE (Bayesian Interval QAE, 2024)
entries.description: Bayesian Interval Quantum Amplitude Estimation (BIQAE): replaces frequentist Clopper-Pearson bounds in IQAE with conjugate Beta(k+1, N-k+1) posterior credible intervals (N_shots=36) and Bayesian posterior-mean terminal readout.

entries.name: IQAE-CP (Grinko et al. 2021)
entries.description: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation with exact Clopper-Pearson beta confidence intervals (Grinko et al. 2021, npj Quantum Inf. 7, 52; arXiv:1912.05559, N_shots=100, r=2, alpha=delta/T).

entries.name: MLAE-EIS (Suzuki et al. 2020)
entries.description: Maximum-Likelihood Amplitude Estimation with the exponentially incremental sequence (EIS) of Suzuki et al. 2020 (Quantum Inf. Process. 19, 75; arXiv:1904.10246), run exactly as in the paper: m_0 = 0, m_k = 2^(k-1) for k = 1..M, N_shot = 100 shots per circuit, exact global maximum-likelihood estimate. The benchmark scale fixes only M, through the deepest circuit 2^(M-1) <= n_max. Queries and errors follow the benchmark conventions (cost n per shot at depth n >= 1, error in a = sin theta).

entries.name: FAE (Nakaji 2020)
entries.description: Faster Amplitude Estimation (Nakaji 2020, Quantum Inf. Comput. 20, 1109; arXiv:2003.02417): two-stage adaptive cosine schedule with doubling Grover depths k_j = 2^{j-1}, Hoeffding confidence intervals, and two-circuit cosine product disambiguation in Stage 2.

entries.name: IQAE-Chernoff (Grinko et al. 2021)
entries.description: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation with Chernoff-Hoeffding confidence intervals (Grinko et al. 2021, npj Quantum Inf. 7, 52; arXiv:1912.05559): adaptive odd-degree Chebyshev interval shrinking with Hoeffding bounds (N_shots=100, r=2, alpha=delta/T).

entries.name: MLAE-LIS (Suzuki et al. 2020)
entries.description: Maximum-Likelihood Amplitude Estimation with the linearly incremental sequence (LIS) of Suzuki et al. 2020 (Quantum Inf. Process. 19, 75; arXiv:1904.10246), run exactly as in the paper: m_k = k for k = 0..M, N_shot = 100 shots per circuit, exact global maximum-likelihood estimate. The benchmark scale fixes only M = n_max. Queries and errors follow the benchmark conventions (cost n per shot at depth n >= 1, error in a = sin theta); the paper's own N_q = sum N_k (2 m_k + 1) and RMSE in sin^2 theta differ by fixed factors.

depth_limited.description: Depth-Limited Regime (max Grover depth capped at M in {64, 256}, total budget B = s * B_0(M) for s in {4, 16, 64}; Labib 2026, arXiv:2609.02715). Reports trade-off constants Ctilde_delta = eps_delta^2 * M * B_tot.

noisy.description: Depolarizing Noise Regime (per-oracle depolarizing rate eta = 1e-3, fringe visibility V_n = (1 - eta)^(2n+1); Labib 2026, arXiv:2609.02715). Compares noise-ignorant and noise-aware non-adaptive schedules, depth-capped uniform scaling, and pair anchors.
